tldr_text:
An American military aircraft fired precision munitions at the Palau-flagged bulk carrier Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday, disabling its propulsion system after the vessel departed the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas. United States Central Command confirmed the civilian crew was unharmed and stated the ship had attempted to run a naval blockade of Iranian ports despite repeated warnings. The Pacific Archer marks the sixth vessel disabled by American forces for violating the Iranian port blockade since its reimposition in July.

Costa Rican migration authorities denied entry to United Nations special rapporteur Francesca Albanese at Juan Santamaria International Airport on Friday, keeping her at the facility for a second night. Omer Badilla, director general of the migration directorate, stated that Albanese was the subject of an international alert over links to terrorist acts and posed a national security risk under the General Law of Migration and Immigration. Albanese had traveled to Costa Rica to receive an honorary doctorate from the state-run University of Costa Rica.

Hackers breached the United States Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform within the past month during system upgrade work, creating operational disruptions across the network. The compromised system hosts critical operational networks including the Cloud One Control Plane, which integrates services from Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, and Alphabet to support personnel, logistics, maintenance, air defense radar, and munitions tracking systems. The intrusion resulted in paused application migrations and blocked updates across the platform.

President Donald Trump defended referring to Russian President Vladimir Putin as a friend during remarks at his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida, stating that personal diplomacy is necessary to reach a deal to end the war in Ukraine. Trump asserted on Truth Social that he urged Putin during meetings in China to pull back military aggression across Europe to achieve a swift settlement. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy publicly criticized the remarks, calling the friendship strange and labeling the Russian leader an aggressor and a killer.

A convoy of Russian ships carrying military vehicles bound for Libya turned around in the Mediterranean after Ukrainian maritime drones sank a Russian naval corvette in Benghazi port on November 22. The convoy, escorted by the Russian navy frigate Golovko, turned back near the Strait of Sicily on the same day as the attack and paused off the coast of Algeria. The sunken corvette Merkury had been accompanying the cargo ship after beginning loading operations.

A security alert instructed United States personnel at the Royal Air Force base in Lakenheath to shelter in place during an incident involving unauthorized drone activity, which officials suspect may be linked to Iran. Neither British nor American personnel recovered any of the drones, leaving authorities unable to determine whether the unmanned aerial systems carried weapons, surveillance equipment, or other payloads. The United Kingdom Ministry of Defense confirmed that Ministry of Defense Police and Suffolk Police worked alongside United States Air Force personnel to resolve the situation without casualties or infrastructure damage.

European Union leaders wrapped up a special two-day summit in Brussels without reaching an agreement on the bloc's seven-year budget for the 2028 to 2034 period, cutting the meeting short after talks broke down late Thursday night. Negotiations stalled as fiscally conservative nations and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz pushed for expenditure cuts and demanded that all twenty-seven member states greenlight an additional forty-five billion euro support loan for Ukraine through 2027 before signing the broader framework. Leaders agreed to reconvene in mid-December to attempt a final agreement before the year-end deadline.

More than 150,000 Amazon customers have emailed City Council members urging them to oppose the Delivery Protection Act since November 19, up from roughly 60,000 emails generated within the campaign's first 36 hours. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani released a video Friday pushing the union-backed legislation on Black Friday, demanding new licensing and employment requirements on delivery operations across the city. Amazon warned customers that the proposed legislation could add up to five dollars per order.

Spain's Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez made a final push on Friday ahead of a weekend general election widely expected to deliver a victory for conservatives and the far right. Polls have consistently put Sanchez behind the main right-wing Popular Party, which is predicted to win the most seats in a hung parliament and could rely on the far-right, anti-immigration Vox party. A campaign banner in Valencia displaying an anti-immigration message from Vox was taken down on Friday following complaints from left-wing parties.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani underwent a successful seventy-minute surgery on Friday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon sustained during a soccer match against the City Hall press corps last week. Press secretary Joe Calvello stated that the mayor was discharged from the hospital and is resting comfortably at Gracie Mansion, with a full recovery expected. First Deputy Mayor Dean Fuleihan led day-to-day city operations while the mayor was hospitalized.
